title: New York Cheesecake
subtitle: dense and creamy baked cheesecake
excerpt: A classic baked cheesecake with a biscuit base and a dense, smooth cream cheese filling. It needs slow baking and patience to set properly. Serve cold, plain or with a fruit compote.
sourceNotes: New York cheesecake became famous through delis and bakeries in Manhattan from the early 20th century. The dense, cream cheese version is distinct from lighter European styles.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze whole or in slices. Thaw overnight in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before and chill overnight. It improves with time in the fridge.

content.text: Do not beat the filling too vigorously -- excess air causes the cheesecake to crack. Once baked, leave the door of the oven ajar and let it cool inside for an hour. Rushing the cooling causes cracks.
Preheat oven to 160C (fan 140C / gas 3). Grease and line a 23cm springform tin.
Mix the crushed biscuits with melted butter. Press firmly into the base of the tin. Chill for 15 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar together until smooth. Do not over-beat.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing gently after each. Stir in the vanilla, lemon zest and juice, and flour.
Pour onto the chilled base. Place the tin on a baking sheet.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until set at the edges but with a slight wobble in the centre.
Spread soured cream over the top. Return to the oven for 10 minutes. Turn off the oven.
Leave in the oven with the door ajar for 1 hour. Then cool completely at room temperature.
Chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours before serving.

items.symptom: Cheesecake has cracks across the top
items.cause: Oven too hot or cooled too quickly
items.fix: Use a water bath next time (place tin in a roasting tray half filled with hot water). Cool slowly in the switched-off oven.

items.symptom: Centre is still runny after chilling
items.fix: A slight wobble when it comes out of the oven is correct -- it sets further as it cools. If very liquid, bake for 10 more minutes.

items.cause: Not enough butter or not pressed firmly
items.fix: Press the base firmly with the back of a spoon and chill before adding the filling.

content.text: New York cheesecake became famous through the Jewish delis and bakeries of Manhattan in the early 20th century. The dense, all-cream-cheese style set it apart from lighter European versions. Junior's Restaurant in Brooklyn has been serving it since 1950 and remains one of the city's most celebrated versions. It is now one of the most recognisable American desserts in the world.
